answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a wander as the anchor of the cost.
